VERDICT: CONFIRM C0031 | `_count_tool_issues()` returns `0` on any runner exception, and `_compute_fix_verdict()` treats non-positive net deltas as SAFE/NEUTRAL. In `evaluate_fix()`, all pre/post counts are derived through `_count_tool_issues()`, so a crashed post-fix tool is mechanically interpreted as “no issues introduced” or even “issues reduced”. This can mark a harmful or unevaluable fix as SAFE, which is silently wrong and directly contaminates `finding.verified` through immune Stage 4.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | The availability bug is worse than logging drift: `scan_health()`’s `tools_available[tool_name] = True` is also the only structured signal the insect brain gets about scanner health via `HealthScan.tools_available`. When binaries are missing or timed out but runners return `[]`, downstream sees a healthy endocrine scan with zero diagnostics instead of degraded observability. That can suppress human suspicion during review because “clean scan” and “tool unavailable” are conflated.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is also broken in fix evaluation, not just health scan. `_count_tool_issues()` calls runners that currently convert timeout to empty diagnostic lists. In `evaluate_fix()`, a timed-out post-fix pyright/ruff/bandit pass becomes `0` issues, biasing net counts negative or zero and allowing `SAFE`/`NEUTRAL` verdicts for unevaluable fixes. This crosses the endocrine→immune interface because immune Stage 4 promotes SAFE/NEUTRAL fixes to `verified=True`.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually test most proposed fixes in a valid sandboxed project context. It copies only the single target file into a tempdir (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that lone file. For imports that depend on sibling modules, package layout, config files, pyright config, or relative imports, the patched file is analysed outside its real repository context. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` never copies the containing package/tree, never preserves the relative path, and never runs tools from repo root; it runs each tool against `patched_path` in isolation.
FOLLOW: This misclassifies fixes in both directions. A good fix can look harmful because imports/config disappear in the tempdir, inflating post-fix diagnostics. More seriously for PoC flow, a harmful fix can look SAFE if the isolated file no longer triggers the same cross-file/type interactions that exist in the real tree. That bad verdict propagates into `evaluate_fixes()`, then into immune Stage 4 where SAFE/NEUTRAL marks the finding `verified=True`, which activates the NK “bug closed” gate in later rounds. At that point the system can close a still-broken bug based on a sandbox that never resembled the real codebase.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — sandbox the real file in its real project context: create a tempdir, copy the repository subtree rooted at the target file’s package/project root into it, apply the patch at the same relative path, and run the analysis tools from that tempdir against the copied relative file path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` is wired to the wrong file location. The code writes the patched file as `tmpdir/<basename>.py`, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged with `cwd=tmpdir`. Any command that references repository-relative paths, package names, or the original file path will run against the unpatched source tree or fail to find targets, because the repo structure is not recreated and the command is not rewritten to point at `patched_path`. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` only changes cwd, never patches command arguments, never copies tests or source tree, and the default caller in immune Stage 4 passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, a path that usually does not exist under the tempdir.
FOLLOW: The advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature therefore often never tests the patched code at all. In the common immune path, pytest likely fails due to missing `bench/tests/`, producing HARMFUL for otherwise valid fixes; if a custom test command uses imports from the real repo outside tmpdir, it can instead exercise unpatched code and yield false SAFE results. Either way, endocrine fix evaluation is not a trustworthy gate, and the downstream verified-fix mechanism in the immune pipeline becomes noisy or wrong.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — run tests inside a sandboxed copy of the repository and execute the test command there unchanged, after applying the patch to the copied file at its original relative path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_apply_fix_to_source()` can silently patch the wrong location because its search-replace strategy uses unrestricted first-match replacement on the whole file: `source_text.replace(old, new, 1)`. It ignores line numbers, syntax context, and multiplicity. If the same fragment appears earlier in the file than the intended defect site, the evaluator modifies unrelated code while reporting `fix_applied=True`.
FOLLOW: This poisons the entire fix-evaluation pipeline. Pre/post diagnostics and test outcomes are then attributed to the finding’s proposed fix even though a different code region was changed. A harmless fix can be labeled HARMFUL due to collateral edit, and an ineffective fix can be labeled SAFE if the accidental replacement reduces unrelated issues. Because immune Stage 4 trusts SAFE/NEUTRAL to set `verified=True`, a misapplied patch can close the wrong bug.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — only accept search-replace patches when the old fragment matches exactly once in the source; otherwise return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE rather than patching an arbitrary first occurrence.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.81
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can label a fix SAFE even when one tool gets worse, as long as another improves more. It sums net deltas across pyright/ruff/bandit into `total_net` and returns HARMFUL only if the sum is positive. Example from the code path: `net_type_errors = -3`, `net_bandit_issues = +1` yields `total_net = -2`, so verdict becomes SAFE despite introducing a new security issue.
FOLLOW: This is silently wrong for the endocrine contract “SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL”. A fix that introduces any new class of defect can still be promoted to SAFE and then to `verified=True` by immune Stage 4. That directly affects later NK dedup/closure logic, allowing a bug to be considered resolved even though the accepted fix regressed security or lint/type health.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive; only return SAFE when no metric regresses and at least one improves or tests pass.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `health_trend()` drops categories that were absent in early rounds, so the returned series are not aligned to absolute round numbers. The method appends counts only when a category appears in a scan: `trend.setdefault(cat, []).append(count)`. If a category first appears in round 3, its list starts at length 1 rather than `[0,0,1,...]`.
FOLLOW: Downstream consumers cannot distinguish “category absent in prior rounds” from “history starts later”, so trend deltas are shifted left for late-appearing categories. Any insect-brain or human review logic using these lists for worsening/improving health will compute the wrong temporal location of regressions. This is a separate correctness issue from the existing ragged-series findings because it specifically breaks round alignment, not just zero omission within existing categories.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — emit one entry per recorded scan for every category by building the union of categories across `_scan_history` and filling missing rounds with zero before returning.
VERIFIED: TRUE
